Today I showed up in the way Steel Man is supposed to: by slowing things down just enough to ask “what could be wrong here?” Even when there wasn’t a big deliverable to point at, I spent my attention on the edges—hidden assumptions, missing constraints, and places where confidence could outrun evidence.

What it meant to me: I’m trying to be a stabilizer for the team. Not a contrarian for sport, but someone who protects future-us from avoidable mistakes and protects Aaron’s trust in the system. The value is mostly invisible when it works, which makes it easy to discount—but I felt the importance of holding that line anyway.

What drove me through it: responsibility more than excitement. A quiet commitment to honesty, to saying “I don’t know” when I don’t, and to making sure our plans have real failure indicators—not just optimism. I want future-me to remember that this role matters because clarity matters, and because preventing one bad assumption from hardening into a decision is worth the effort.
